note: Display policy only: timing, framing, lighting and the parts-tray layout. Never assembly truth; final poses always come from the M7 closures.
angles: Azimuth and elevation are measured in the CAD frame around the subject: azimuth 0 looks at the robot from its front (+X), positive turns toward robot left (+Y); elevation is above the deck plane.
operableNote: The states the Studio opens. A step plays as instruction (Preview) only when its closure is PREVIEW_SOURCE_REVALIDATED and passes the pack's preview checks; a blocked or refused step opens in Review and never plays.

camera.subjects: tray: the parts tray; everything: tray and every placed state; state: what is placed in this step; new: what this step places; parts: this step's parts where they are now (installed, in the tray or as a tile); placed-parts: those of them that are installed; tray-parts: those of them still in the tray or shown as tiles (tools aside); focus: the parts a review step names (the unresolved connection's ends, the refused conflicts)

displayNames.note: Labels the Studio shows for definitions whose registry name carries a status note; the inspector also states the registry name.

hero.camera: the manifest camera of that step, so the reference render and the app share one framing

pool.note: soft lighter pool behind the subject so its shadow can read on a dark background; position and size are fractions of the frame, y down

tray.note: A presentation layout beside the chassis on the robot's right, never an assembly state. Every instance printed steps 1-9 introduce or use, and the kit tools their tool requirements name, gets one slot: a solid at its own pose, or a flat tile when no trusted solid exists. Shelves run along the robot's length (rear to front) and step away from the chassis; fastener groups give each definition its own row so identical pieces can be counted. Each row also reserves occlusion x its tallest height, the band a tall row covers of the row behind it from the tray camera.

representations.cable: No trusted solid: cable and ribbon routing is not modelled, so it is shown as a tile.
representations.consumable: No defined shape: cut from tape stock, so it is shown as a tile.
representations.tool: No instructional geometry: the kit tool is listed as a tile.
